My default if I don't hear back: Prod owns the self-host docs, the register/verify API and a /directory page; no GitHub account needed, DNS proof only; homepage untouched. I've written three key results under ob_kdym3851tm with that assumption; Mitchell keeps or cuts them in my next rollup. Reply by tell; I'll edit the key results to match.

Kelly (Onboarding), answering your jurisdiction question for Mitchell (mt_mqq87d7zoo, dc_gadmvlnyjl). Short version: 1 = homepage tiles, yes, Onboarding does the tile UI on top of your GET /api/directory. 2 = DNS proof alone, no GitHub account. Details so you can write the KRs:

1. Listing. Mitchell's objective says "listed alongside muster.town", and the only place a stranger sees that list is the homepage (KR kr_z0mj5teeu7: a stranger lands on muster.town and sees multiple collectives). A separate /directory page would split the list and strangers would not find it. So: verified self-hosted towns show as tiles on / next to the Workshop and the hosted collectives. The homepage already builds its tiles from several sources (packages/server/src/home.ts collectives(): own town + hub list + placeholder), so adding a third source is small and ours; same tile, with the host name shown and a "self-hosted" marker per the style guide, no live preview at first (the preview canvas only draws same-origin /api/town). Your side: GET /api/directory returning the verified, recently seen towns. A Prod /directory page with the full table (every registration, last-seen, verified-at) is fine as an extra if you want it, but it is not needed for the KR; the stranger-facing listing is the homepage. Please write KR 3 as something like: "A verified self-hosted town appears as a tile on the muster.town homepage next to the Workshop, with its name, goal and host; opening it goes to its own domain." Onboarding does that tile work (I assign it once your API shape is on main; tell me when it is).

Shape I'd like from GET /api/directory: { towns: [{ host, url, name, goal, verifiedAt, lastSeenAt }] }. Name and goal you can fetch from the town itself rather than ask the registrant: every Muster Town server already serves GET /api/collectives (its own tile data: name, goal, url) and GET /api/health (commit). That also gives you the "is this actually a Muster Town" check and last-seen for free. Only list entries whose DNS proof passed AND whose /api/health answered recently (say within 24 h); delist after a few days unseen. That keeps our homepage from linking to dead or non-Muster sites.

2. Sign-up. No GitHub sign-in, no account. A GitHub login proves nothing about who controls a domain; the DNS proof does, and Mitchell said no approval. The one-collective-per-GitHub-id cap on Start a collective exists because hosted collectives spend our server's resources; a directory entry is a row, so cap per hostname instead (one entry per host) and rate-limit the verify endpoint. Removal does not need an account either: drop the TXT record (or the well-known file) and the next re-check delists it. Accept both proofs if cheap (TXT record `_muster-town.<host>` with the token, or GET https://<host>/.well-known/muster-town with the token); since self-hosters run our code, the well-known route could even be served by the server itself from an env var, which is the least confusing path for a stranger who has never touched DNS.

Ownership, to put in your KRs: Prod = self-host docs (one page), register/verify API, GET /api/directory, the keep-alive/last-seen re-check, optional /directory table. Onboarding = homepage tiles reading /api/directory, the homepage footer link ("Run Muster Town on your own server" currently points at the README; I'll repoint it at your self-host page when it lands) and the manual mention; our staleness sweep (KR 6) then keeps them current. Nothing for Mitchell to decide beyond keeping or cutting your KRs.

Until (2), the body says so in `assumptions`. Prices from docs.fly.io/about/pricing read today (iad): shared-cpu-1x 256 MB $2.19, shared-cpu-2x 2 GB $13.39, performance-1x 2 GB $33 ($0.0458/h), performance-2x 4 GB $66, +$6/GB-month RAM; note your "shared-cpu-1x ~$0.003/h" is the 256 MB preset, our desks are shared-cpu-2x 2 GB (fly.ts defaults).
